description: Solo team building a terrain aware lunar mission decision support browser. Using NASA LRO LOLA elevation models and JPL Horizons ephemeris, the tool computes local horizon obstructions, solar illumination windows, and geometric Direct-to-Earth visibility trade-offs across lunar South Pole landing sites.
summary: LOLA Horizon is a terrain aware lunar south pole mission decision support browser built for the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. At the lunar south pole (75°S–90°S), the Sun and Earth hover just degrees above the horizon, meaning surrounding crater rims and launch-date slips can turn a viable site into a multi-day communications blackout. Using NASA LRO LOLA elevation models (LDEM_75S_240M) and NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441) ephemerides, LOLA Horizon computes 360° topographic horizon masks, solar illumination windows, Direct-to-Earth (DTE) blackout durations, and launch-slip sensitivity across candidate CLPS landing sites and mission dates—exposing transparent physical margins instead of arbitrary black-box scores.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS?

LOLA Horizon evaluates candidate Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) landing sites near the lunar south pole across multiple launch windows:

1. 360° Topographic Horizon Masking: Extracts 1°-resolution horizon obstruction silhouettes from NASA PDS LRO LOLA Gridded Data Records (LDEM_75S_240M, 240 m/px).

2. Topocentric Ephemeris Integration: Queries NASA/JPL Horizons (DE441, coord@301) at 15-minute cadence (1,345 steps over 14.0 Earth days) for Malapert A (-80.13°S, 1.44°E), Mons Mouton (-84.90°S, 31.00°E), and Shackleton Connecting Ridge (-89.68°S, 197.00°E) across three windows: IM-1 Historical Validation (Feb 2024), Nov 2026 Live Window, and Feb 2027 (+3 Month Launch Slip).

3. Interactive Mission Console: Users can scrub the 14-day timeline, toggle Solar Center vs. Upper-Limb (+0.267°) models, adjust DTE elevation clearance cutoffs (0°–15°), inspect the 360° Polar Horizon Obstruction Radar, explore a Three.js 3D Lunar Globe (explicitly marked as contextual visualization only), and compare sites side by side.

KEY FINDING & IMPACT

In Nov 2026, both Malapert A and Mons Mouton maintain 100.0% Earth DTE visibility (336.3 h, 0.0 h blackout). Under a 3-month launch slip to Feb 2027, Mons Mouton retains more sunlight (269.0 h vs. 245.5 h) but suffers a 158.8-hour (~6.6-day) Earth blackout (52.8% DTE), whereas Malapert A retains 82.8% DTE (278.5 h, max blackout 57.8 h). Instead of inventing arbitrary 0–100 scores, LOLA Horizon lets mission planners audit exact physical margins.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES & CREATIVITY

- Frontend: Next.js 16, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js (WebGL 3D globe), Lucide Icons.

- Science Engine & QA: Python 3.13, NumPy, Rasterio, Pytest (12/12 unit & dataset tests passing).

- Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment: AI coding assistance was used during development to accelerate frontend UI scaffolding, Three.js visualization, and documentation; all scientific visibility and continuity calculations are deterministic and verified by the Python test suite.
